_readme: Every legal value the site uses lives here, never in the code. Each value was read on the official source cited below on retrieved_at. Data figures (medians, claims) live in national.json, states.json and counties.json, built by scripts/build-data.py.

caps._basis: 42 U.S.C. 4015(e): yearly increase of the risk premium for an individual property capped at 18 %; 42 U.S.C. 4015(c): 25 % a year for non-primary residences, business properties, severe repetitive loss and substantially damaged or improved buildings. The cap applies to the premium, not to the Federal Policy Fee or the HFIAA surcharge.

fees._basis: FEMA Flood Insurance Manual, October 2025 edition, Section 3.II.F (Tables 33 to 36), unchanged by bulletin W-26001 (December 1, 2026). Fees and surcharges are not part of the full-risk or discounted premium; the yearly cap sits inside the discounted premium.

limits._basis: 42 U.S.C. 4013(b), 44 CFR 61.6, FEMA Flood Insurance Manual Table 24: one-to-four family homes 250,000 building and 100,000 contents; non-residential 500,000 and 500,000; ICC pays up to 30,000.

deductibles._basis: 42 U.S.C. 4013(d)(1) and FEMA Flood Insurance Manual Table 26: building options 1,000 (coverage up to 100,000) or 1,250 (above), 2,000, 5,000, 10,000; contents 1,000, 2,000, 5,000, 10,000. residentialDefault is only the starting value of the calculator, one of the legal options.

waiting._basis: 42 U.S.C. 4013(c), 44 CFR 61.11 and FEMA Flood Insurance Manual 2.III: 30 days; none at a loan closing; 1 day in the 13 months after a map revision that newly places the building in a high-risk area (the statute says 1 year); 1 day after a wildfire on federal land within 60 days of containment.
